The semicircle on the right has a curved half-circumference plus its straight diameter. Area formulas count the interior and use square units.

task: Find cuboid volume or covering area
formula: V=lwh; closed SA=2(lw+lh+wh). 1 cm³=1 mL; 1000 cm³=1 L.
condition: Volume fills the box; surface area covers its faces.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Find cuboid volume or covering area. Length, width and height multiply to count the space inside the box."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><polygon points="135,64 310,64 310,145 135,145" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5" /><polygon points="135,64 195,23 370,23 310,64" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2.5" /><polygon points="310,64 370,23 370,104 310,145" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2.5" /></g><text x="222.15" y="158.5" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="24" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">l</text><text x="365.8" y="121.95" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="24" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">w</text><text x="131.2" y="106.65" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="24" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">h</text></svg>
narration: Length, width and height multiply to count the space inside the box. For a closed covering, pair the front and back, top and bottom, and two ends. Add those six face areas. Convert capacity using one cubic centimetre per millilitre and one thousand cubic centimetres per litre.

task: Remove hidden faces when joining solids
formula: Exposed SA=SA₁+SA₂−2A_shared; volumes add when solids do not overlap.
condition: One full shared face is hidden on BOTH solids.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Remove hidden faces when joining solids. The amber join lies inside the completed solid."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><rect x="48" y="40" width="190" height="102" rx="5" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" /><rect x="238" y="40" width="190" height="102" rx="5" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2" /><line x1="238" y1="40" x2="238" y2="142" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="7" /><line x1="148" y1="87" x2="222" y2="87" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M214.97933950487703,90.83540430883363 L222,87 L214.97933950487703,83.16459569116637" stroke="#b96a12" fill="none" stroke-width="2.5" /><line x1="328" y1="87" x2="254" y2="87" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M261.02066049512297,83.16459569116637 L254,87 L261.02066049512297,90.83540430883362" stroke="#b96a12" fill="none" stroke-width="2.5" /></g><text x="240.0" y="161.05" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="22" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">two touching faces become internal</text></svg>
narration: The amber join lies inside the completed solid. If you start by adding the surface areas of the separate solids, you have counted this same contact region twice: once on each solid. Remove both hidden faces. Volumes can simply be added provided the solids do not overlap.

task: Multiply cross-section area by length
formula: V=A_cross×L; L=V/A_cross, where A_cross>0.
condition: Find the end area first; a triangular end needs the factor ½.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Multiply cross-section area by length. The triangular end repeats unchanged along the prism’s length."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><polygon points="62,132 172,132 115,43" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5" /><polygon points="172,132 382,108 325,19 115,43" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2.5" /><line x1="62" y1="132" x2="272" y2="108" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="5 5" /><line x1="272" y1="108" x2="382" y2="108" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="5 5" /><line x1="272" y1="108" x2="325" y2="19" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="5 5" /></g><text x="132.05" y="151.7" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#087f75" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="283.35" y="138.1" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#3175ba" text-anchor="middle">L</text><text x="265.5" y="74.35" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="20" fill="#3175ba" text-anchor="middle">same end area</text></svg>
narration: The triangular end repeats unchanged along the prism’s length. Find that one cross-section area, then multiply by the distance between the ends. To recover a missing length, divide volume by the end area. Using a triangle’s base times height without halving would double the result.

task: Cover a closed right prism
formula: SA=2A_cross+P_cross×L.
condition: For a closed right prism: two ends plus all side rectangles.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Cover a closed right prism. The prism has two identical end faces."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><polygon points="62,132 172,132 115,43" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5" /><polygon points="172,132 382,108 325,19 115,43" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2.5" /><line x1="62" y1="132" x2="272" y2="108" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="5 5" /><line x1="272" y1="108" x2="382" y2="108" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="5 5" /><line x1="272" y1="108" x2="325" y2="19" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="5 5" /></g><text x="132.05" y="151.7" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#087f75" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="283.35" y="138.1" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#3175ba" text-anchor="middle">L</text><text x="263.8" y="74.35" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="20" fill="#3175ba" text-anchor="middle">3 side faces</text></svg>
narration: The prism has two identical end faces. Its side rectangles unwrap into a strip whose width is the perimeter of the cross-section and whose length is the prism length. Add the two end areas to this rectangular strip area, keeping perimeter and area quantities distinct.

task: Convert a map length both ways
formula: At scale 1:n: real=n×drawing; drawing=real/n.
condition: Convert to the same units before applying the ratio.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Convert a map length both ways. One unit on the drawing corresponds to n of the same units in reality."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><line x1="48" y1="75" x2="168" y2="75" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="4" /><line x1="48" y1="60" x2="48" y2="90" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2" /><line x1="168" y1="60" x2="168" y2="90" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2" /><line x1="189" y1="74" x2="261" y2="74" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M253.97933950487703,77.83540430883363 L261,74 L253.97933950487703,70.16459569116637" stroke="#173349" fill="none" stroke-width="2.5" /><line x1="282" y1="75" x2="442" y2="75" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="4" /><line x1="282" y1="60" x2="282" y2="90" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" /><line x1="442" y1="60" x2="442" y2="90" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" /></g><text x="127.8" y="116.85" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="22" fill="#3175ba" text-anchor="middle">drawing</text><text x="227.25" y="52.25" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="24" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">×n</text><text x="343.7" y="116.85" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="22" fill="#087f75" text-anchor="middle">real</text><text x="240.0" y="155.95" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="21" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">Reverse the arrow by dividing by n.</text></svg>
narration: One unit on the drawing corresponds to n of the same units in reality. Multiply a drawing length by n to obtain the real length, or divide the real length by n to draw it. Convert centimetres, metres or kilometres before comparing the two sides of the ratio.

task: Scale lengths, areas, volumes and costs
formula: Length factor k → area factor k², volume factor k³. Cost=quantity×unit price.
condition: Use square or cubic factors for square or cubic units.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Scale lengths, areas, volumes and costs. Doubling both dimensions makes four copies of the original square, so the area grows by four."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><rect x="39" y="70" width="52" height="52" rx="5" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" /><rect x="160" y="18" width="104" height="104" rx="5" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2" /><line x1="212" y1="18" x2="212" y2="122" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2" /><line x1="160" y1="70" x2="264" y2="70" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2" /></g><text x="91.25" y="147.45" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="20" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">1 square</text><text x="216.2" y="147.45" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="20" fill="#3175ba" text-anchor="middle">4 squares</text><text x="354.75" y="65.0" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="24" fill="#087f75" text-anchor="middle">length ×2</text><text x="354.75" y="101.55" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="24" fill="#3175ba" text-anchor="middle">area ×4</text><text x="354.75" y="138.1" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="23" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">volume ×8</text></svg>
narration: Doubling both dimensions makes four copies of the original square, so the area grows by four. Doubling three dimensions would make eight copies of a solid. Choose the linear, square or cubic scale factor to match the quantity, then multiply by the stated unit price for a cost.

task: Find the mode and ordered median
formula: Mode=most frequent. Odd N: position (N+1)/2. Even N: mean of positions N/2 and N/2+1.
condition: Sort first. There may be several modes or no unique mode.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Find the mode and ordered median. The observations are already ordered, so the third of five values is the median."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><rect x="35" y="52" width="72" height="62" rx="5" fill="#f0f7f6" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" /><rect x="118" y="52" width="72" height="62" rx="5" fill="#f0f7f6" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" /><rect x="201" y="52" width="72" height="62" rx="5" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2" /><rect x="284" y="52" width="72" height="62" rx="5" fill="#f0f7f6" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" /><rect x="367" y="52" width="72" height="62" rx="5" fill="#f0f7f6" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" /></g><text x="96.35" y="92.2" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="29" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">2</text><text x="166.9" y="92.2" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="29" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">4</text><text x="237.45" y="92.2" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="29" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">4</text><text x="308.0" y="92.2" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="29" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">7</text><text x="378.55" y="92.2" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="29" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">9</text><text x="240.0" y="144.05" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="23" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">middle = 4; most frequent = 4</text></svg>
narration: The observations are already ordered, so the third of five values is the median. Four also appears most often, making it the mode in this example. With an even number of observations, average the two middle values. A mode may be shared by several values.

task: Recover a total or missing observation
formula: Mean=total/N; total=N×mean; missing=required total−known total.
condition: N includes the missing observations.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Recover a total or missing observation. A mean of six across four observations requires a total of twenty-four."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><rect x="31" y="40" width="418" height="47" rx="5" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" /><rect x="40" y="111" width="80" height="45" rx="5" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" /><rect x="145" y="111" width="80" height="45" rx="5" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" /><rect x="250" y="111" width="80" height="45" rx="5" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" /><rect x="355" y="111" width="85" height="45" rx="5" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2" /></g><text x="240.0" y="75.2" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="22" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">4 observations × mean 6 = total 24</text><text x="104.0" y="133.85" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="26" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">3</text><text x="193.25" y="133.85" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="26" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">5</text><text x="282.5" y="133.85" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="26" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">7</text><text x="373.45" y="133.85" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="26" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">9 ?</text></svg>
narration: A mean of six across four observations requires a total of twenty-four. The three known observations add to fifteen, leaving nine for the missing value. Count all four observations when constructing the required total. Finally, insert the answer and recompute the mean to check it.

task: Combine group means with their sizes
formula: Combined mean=Σ(n×group mean)/Σn.
condition: Weight each mean by its group size.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Combine group means with their sizes. Convert each group’s mean back into its total: three times eight gives twenty-four, and two times thirteen gives twenty-six."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><rect x="35" y="45" width="205" height="66" rx="5" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2" /><rect x="245" y="45" width="200" height="66" rx="5" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2" /></g><text x="152.45" y="72" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="23" fill="#087f75" text-anchor="middle">3 people</text><text x="152.45" y="103" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="23" fill="#087f75" text-anchor="middle">mean 8</text><text x="329.25" y="72" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="23" fill="#3175ba" text-anchor="middle">2 people</text><text x="329.25" y="103" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="23" fill="#3175ba" text-anchor="middle">mean 13</text><text x="240.0" y="148.3" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="27" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">(3×8 + 2×13)/5 = 10</text></svg>
narration: Convert each group’s mean back into its total: three times eight gives twenty-four, and two times thirteen gives twenty-six. Add these totals and divide by all five people. Giving the two means equal weight would ignore the different numbers of observations they summarise.

task: Choose an average that answers the question
formula: Mean: all values. Median: middle, resistant to extremes. Mode: most common value or category.
condition: Justify the choice in context; no average is always best.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Choose an average that answers the question. An extreme lies far from the main cluster."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><line x1="42" y1="95" x2="443" y2="95" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M435.97933950487703,98.83540430883363 L443,95 L435.97933950487703,91.16459569116637" stroke="#173349" fill="none" stroke-width="2.5" /><line x1="60.0" y1="88" x2="60.0" y2="102" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2" /><line x1="151.25" y1="88" x2="151.25" y2="102" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2" /><line x1="242.5" y1="88" x2="242.5" y2="102" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2" /><line x1="333.75" y1="88" x2="333.75" y2="102" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2" /><line x1="425.0" y1="88" x2="425.0" y2="102" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2" /><circle cx="95" cy="95" r="6" fill="#087f75" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5" /><circle cx="130" cy="95" r="6" fill="#087f75" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5" /><circle cx="165" cy="95" r="6" fill="#087f75" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5" /><circle cx="425" cy="95" r="8" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2.5" /></g><text x="87.0" y="124.5" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="21" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">2</text><text x="164.562" y="124.5" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="21" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">4</text><text x="242.125" y="124.5" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="21" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">6</text><text x="319.688" y="124.5" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="21" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">8</text><text x="397.25" y="124.5" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="21" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">10</text><text x="388.75" y="59.9" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="20" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">extreme</text><text x="240.0" y="152.55" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="20" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">An extreme pulls the mean towards it.</text></svg>
narration: Most values form a cluster, while the distant amber point is an extreme. The mean responds strongly because it includes every value in its total. The median depends on the middle position and is more resistant. Choose and justify the measure that best represents the feature being discussed.

task: Weight values by their frequencies
formula: Mean=Σfx/Σf.
condition: A value repeated f times contributes f×x to the total.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Weight values by their frequencies. The frequency column says that two occurs three times and five occurs twice."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><line x1="40" y1="44" x2="440" y2="44" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2" /></g><text x="106.55" y="42.9" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="24" fill="#087f75" text-anchor="middle">x</text><text x="240.0" y="42.9" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="24" fill="#3175ba" text-anchor="middle">f</text><text x="373.45" y="42.9" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="24" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">fx</text><text x="106.55" y="82.0" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">2</text><text x="240.0" y="82.0" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">3</text><text x="373.45" y="82.0" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">6</text><text x="106.55" y="115.15" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">5</text><text x="240.0" y="115.15" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">2</text><text x="373.45" y="115.15" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">10</text><text x="240.0" y="155.1" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="24" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">mean = (6+10)/(3+2) = 3.2</text></svg>
narration: The frequency column says that two occurs three times and five occurs twice. Their contributions to the total are six and ten. Add the product column and divide by the total frequency, five. Averaging just the two distinct values would discard how often each one occurs.

task: Estimate a mean from intervals
formula: Midpoint=(lower+upper)/2; estimated mean=Σ(f×midpoint)/Σf.
condition: The midpoint represents unknown individual values, so the mean is an estimate.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Estimate a mean from intervals. The interval from ten to twenty is represented by its midpoint, fifteen."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><line x1="55" y1="82" x2="425" y2="82" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="4" /><line x1="55" y1="70" x2="55" y2="94" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2" /><line x1="425" y1="70" x2="425" y2="94" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2" /><circle cx="240" cy="82" r="7" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2.5" /></g><text x="82.75" y="116.85" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="23" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">10</text><text x="397.25" y="116.85" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="23" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">20</text><text x="240.0" y="116.85" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">15</text><text x="240.0" y="45.45" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="21" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">replace this interval by its midpoint</text><text x="240.0" y="155.1" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="21" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">midpoint × frequency → estimated total</text></svg>
narration: The interval from ten to twenty is represented by its midpoint, fifteen. Treat each observation in that interval as if it were fifteen, multiply by the interval’s frequency, and repeat for the other intervals. Divide the estimated total by the observation count; individual values remain unknown.

task: Use the range to find an extreme
formula: Range=max−min; max=min+range; min=max−range.
condition: Check the resulting minimum and maximum against every other value.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Use the range to find an extreme. task: Check whether all statistics can hold
formula: Test total, ordering, median, range and integer conditions together. One contradiction rules the claim out.
condition: A plausible average alone does not prove a data set exists.

Check the minimum and maximum against the claimed range, and retain any integer restrictions. A valid construction must satisfy all these conditions at once; one contradiction is enough to reject it.

task: Find angles on lines and transversals
formula: Straight=180°; turn=360°; vertical opposites equal. Parallel lines: corresponding/alternate equal; same-side interiors sum 180°.
condition: State the parallel-line condition before using F, Z or interior-angle rules.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Find angles on lines and transversals. The arrow marks state that the green lines are parallel."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><line x1="40" y1="48" x2="440" y2="48" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3" /><line x1="40" y1="132" x2="440" y2="132" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3" /><line x1="140" y1="162" x2="329" y2="19" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="3" /><path d="M89 43 L99 48 L89 53" stroke="#087f75" fill="none" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M89 127 L99 132 L89 137" stroke="#087f75" fill="none" stroke-width="2.5" /></g><text x="297.8" y="81.15" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="27" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">a</text><text x="198.35" y="109.2" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="27" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">a</text><text x="370.05" y="156.8" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="20" fill="#087f75" text-anchor="middle">parallel</text></svg>
narration: The arrow marks state that the green lines are parallel. The blue transversal creates equal alternate angles in the Z-shaped arrangement. Other positions give corresponding equality or same-side interior angles adding to one hundred and eighty degrees. The parallel marks justify these relationships; appearance alone does not.

task: Link triangle interiors and an exterior angle
formula: a+b+c=180°; exterior angle=a+b for the two remote interiors.
condition: The adjacent interior is not part of the remote-angle sum.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Link triangle interiors and an exterior angle. The three interior angles add to one hundred and eighty degrees."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><polygon points="65,139 319,139 183,29" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5" /><line x1="319" y1="139" x2="441" y2="139" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="3" /><path d="M350 139 A31 31 0 0 0 341 116" stroke="#b96a12" fill="none" stroke-width="2.5" /></g><text x="130.35" y="123.65" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#087f75" text-anchor="middle">a</text><text x="193.25" y="70.95" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#087f75" text-anchor="middle">b</text><text x="273.15" y="123.65" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">c</text><text x="354.75" y="108.35" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">a+b</text></svg>
narration: The three interior angles add to one hundred and eighty degrees. Extending the base makes an exterior angle beside the interior angle c. Since those adjacent angles also make a straight angle, the exterior equals the other two triangle angles, a plus b.

task: Use only the quadrilateral properties given
formula: Simple quadrilateral: interior sum=360°. Parallelogram: opposite sides/angles equal; adjacent angles sum 180°.
condition: A rhombus need not have right angles; do not add unstated properties.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Use only the quadrilateral properties given. The sloping parallelogram has equal opposite angles, labelled a and b in pairs."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><polygon points="57,139 327,139 423,37 153,37" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5" /><line x1="185" y1="32" x2="185" y2="42" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3" /><line x1="184" y1="134" x2="184" y2="144" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3" /></g><text x="124.4" y="120.25" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">a</text><text x="306.3" y="120.25" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#3175ba" text-anchor="middle">b</text><text x="354.75" y="73.5" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">a</text><text x="177.1" y="73.5" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#3175ba" text-anchor="middle">b</text><text x="240.0" y="160.2" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="24" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">a+b=180°; 2a+2b=360°</text></svg>
narration: The sloping parallelogram has equal opposite angles, labelled a and b in pairs. Adjacent angles add to one hundred and eighty degrees, so all four add to three hundred and sixty. Extra properties such as four right angles require extra information; equal sides alone do not establish them.

task: Match triangles with a valid congruence test
formula: SSS; SAS (included angle); ASA; RHS (right triangles).
condition: AAA gives similarity; SSA is not a general congruence test.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Match triangles with a valid congruence test. The two marked sides and the angle between them match in both triangles."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><polygon points="45,142 194,142 104,34" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5" /><polygon points="284,142 433,142 343,34" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2.5" /><line x1="111" y1="137" x2="111" y2="147" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="4" /><line x1="350" y1="137" x2="350" y2="147" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="4" /><line x1="72" y1="86" x2="83" y2="92" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="4" /><line x1="311" y1="86" x2="322" y2="92" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="4" /><path d="M72 142 A27 27 0 0 0 59 117" stroke="#b96a12" fill="none" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M311 142 A27 27 0 0 0 298 117" stroke="#b96a12" fill="none" stroke-width="2.5" /></g><text x="240.0" y="159.35" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="21" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">SAS: angle between the marked sides</text></svg>
narration: The two marked sides and the angle between them match in both triangles. That is side-angle-side congruence, so corresponding parts are equal. Always name the correspondence and the exact test. Matching only three angles establishes shape, while two sides and a non-included angle may remain ambiguous.

task: Find a side in a right triangle
formula: c²=a²+b²; c=√(a²+b²); a=√(c²−b²).
condition: c is opposite the 90° angle. Take the square root for a length.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Find a side in a right triangle. The right-angle marker identifies the two shorter sides, a and b."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><polygon points="115,138 365,138 365,34" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M349 138 L349 122 L365 122" stroke="#173349" fill="none" stroke-width="2.5" /></g><text x="240.0" y="155.95" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="24" fill="#087f75" text-anchor="middle">a</text><text x="367.5" y="93.9" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="24" fill="#087f75" text-anchor="middle">b</text><text x="233.2" y="73.5" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="24" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">c</text></svg>
narration: The right-angle marker identifies the two shorter sides, a and b. The opposite side c is the hypotenuse. Add the squares to find c, or subtract the known shorter-side square from c squared to find the other shorter side. Take the positive square root for the required length.

task: Find a cuboid’s space diagonal
formula: d=√(l²+w²); D=√(d²+h²)=√(l²+w²+h²).
condition: Use Pythagoras twice; an edge route is longer than the straight diagonal.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Find a cuboid’s space diagonal. First use the two floor edges to find the floor diagonal."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><polygon points="135,64 310,64 310,145 135,145" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5" /><polygon points="135,64 195,23 370,23 310,64" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2.5" /><polygon points="310,64 370,23 370,104 310,145" fill="#fff3dd" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2.5" /><line x1="135" y1="145" x2="370" y2="104" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="3" stroke-dasharray="5 5" /><line x1="135" y1="145" x2="370" y2="23" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="3" /></g><text x="222.15" y="158.5" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="24" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">l</text><text x="365.8" y="121.95" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="24" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">w</text><text x="131.2" y="106.65" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="24" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">h</text><text x="265" y="109" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="22" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">D</text></svg>
narration: First use the two floor edges to find the floor diagonal. That diagonal and the vertical height form a second right triangle whose hypotenuse is the amber space diagonal. Combining the two calculations gives the square root of the sum of the three squared dimensions.

task: Build a proof from accepted reasons
formula: Definition=meaning; axiom=starting fact; theorem=proved fact; converse=reversed implication; corollary=direct consequence.
condition: Equal-looking angles in a sketch do not prove equality.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Build a proof from accepted reasons. At the crossing, a and b form a straight angle, and c and b form another straight angle."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><line x1="40" y1="42" x2="440" y2="142" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3" /><line x1="70" y1="151" x2="410" y2="29" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="3" /></g><text x="233.2" y="56.5" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#3175ba" text-anchor="middle">b</text><text x="189.0" y="98.15" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">a</text><text x="291.0" y="94.75" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">c</text><text x="240.0" y="161.9" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="22" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">a+b=180° and c+b=180° → a=c</text></svg>
narration: At the crossing, a and b form a straight angle, and c and b form another straight angle. Both totals equal one hundred and eighty degrees. Subtract the common angle b to prove a equals c. Each step needs a stated reason, rather than trust in the sketch.

task: Connect equal sides and opposite angles
formula: AB=AC ⇔ ∠ABC=∠ACB in triangle ABC.
condition: Forward theorem and converse require their own justification.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Connect equal sides and opposite angles. The matching side marks show AB equals AC, so the opposite base angles at B and C are equal."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><polygon points="99,143 381,143 240,25" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5" /><line x1="163" y1="77" x2="174" y2="88" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="4" /><line x1="306" y1="88" x2="317" y2="77" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="4" /><path d="M131 143 A32 32 0 0 0 123 123" stroke="#3175ba" fill="none" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M349 143 A32 32 0 0 1 357 123" stroke="#3175ba" fill="none" stroke-width="2.5" /></g><text x="240.0" y="32.7" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="21" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="102.3" y="154.25" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="22" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="376.85" y="154.25" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="22" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">C</text><text x="240.0" y="104.95" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="22" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">equal sides</text></svg>
narration: The matching side marks show AB equals AC, so the opposite base angles at B and C are equal. The converse starts with the equal angles and concludes equal opposite sides. A proof may introduce an angle bisector or a suitable pair of congruent triangles to justify the connection.

task: Prove parallelism from matching angle positions
formula: Equal alternate angles ⇒ parallel lines. Parallel lines ⇔ equal corresponding angles.
condition: The equal angles must occupy the required transversal positions.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Prove parallelism from matching angle positions. The two amber angles are in corresponding positions: the same side of the transversal and the same relative position at each crossing."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><line x1="40" y1="48" x2="440" y2="48" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3" /><line x1="40" y1="132" x2="440" y2="132" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="3" /><line x1="154" y1="166" x2="329" y2="14" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="3" /></g><text x="303.75" y="47.15" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">a</text><text x="219.6" y="116.85" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">a</text><text x="240.0" y="159.35" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="20" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">matching corresponding angles → parallel</text></svg>
narration: The two amber angles are in corresponding positions: the same side of the transversal and the same relative position at each crossing. If these angles are equal, the lines are parallel. Parallel lines also guarantee the equality. Arbitrary equal angles elsewhere would not establish this conclusion.

task: Use the bisecting diagonals of a parallelogram
formula: If diagonals AC and BD meet at E: AE=CE and BE=DE.
condition: The two complete diagonals need not have equal lengths.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Use the bisecting diagonals of a parallelogram. The diagonals cross at E."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><polygon points="48,140 329,140 433,35 152,35" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5" /><line x1="48" y1="140" x2="433" y2="35" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="3" /><line x1="329" y1="140" x2="152" y2="35" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="3" /><circle cx="240.5" cy="87.5" r="5" fill="#173349" stroke="#173349" stroke-width="2.5" /></g><text x="62.35" y="154.25" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="22" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="331.8" y="154.25" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="22" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="419.35" y="41.2" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="22" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">C</text><text x="149.05" y="34.4" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="22" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">D</text><text x="243.4" y="115.15" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="23" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">E</text><text x="122.7" y="104.95" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#3175ba" text-anchor="middle">½</text><text x="351.35" y="76.05" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#3175ba" text-anchor="middle">½</text></svg>
narration: The diagonals cross at E. Each diagonal is divided into two equal halves: AE equals CE, and BE equals DE. Use alternate angles from the parallel sides and equal opposite sides to compare the relevant triangles. Bisecting does not mean the two whole diagonals have equal lengths.

task: Match corresponding sides in similar triangles
formula: AB/PQ=AC/PR=BC/QR; A↔P, B↔Q, C↔R.
condition: Match corresponding vertices or opposite angles before forming ratios.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 180" role="img" aria-label="Match corresponding sides in similar triangles. The corresponding vertices are A with P, B with Q, and C with R."><rect width="480" height="180" fill="#ffffff" /><g transform="translate(36 14) scale(0.85)"><polygon points="40,138 182,138 111,45" fill="#e8f5f1" stroke="#087f75" stroke-width="2.5" /><polygon points="252,147 442,147 347,23" fill="#edf4fc" stroke="#3175ba" stroke-width="2.5" /><line x1="194" y1="104" x2="272" y2="104" stroke="#b96a12" stroke-width="2.5" /><path d="M264.97933950487703,107.83540430883363 L272,104 L264.97933950487703,100.16459569116637" stroke="#b96a12" fill="none" stroke-width="2.5" /></g><text x="130.35" y="45.45" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="21" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="59.8" y="151.7" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="21" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="199.2" y="151.7" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="21" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">C</text><text x="330.95" y="32.7" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="21" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">P</text><text x="239.15" y="159.35" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="21" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">Q</text><text x="422.75" y="159.35" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="21" fill="#173349" text-anchor="middle">R</text><text x="240.0" y="84.55" font-family="DejaVu Sans" font-size="25" fill="#b96a12" text-anchor="middle">× k</text></svg>
narration: The corresponding vertices are A with P, B with Q, and C with R. Every matching side changes by the same scale factor, although the triangles need not have equal size. Form all ratios in a consistent direction. A proof connects equal corresponding angles with these proportional sides.

task: Test whether a triangle is right-angled
formula: If c is longest and c²=a²+b², the angle opposite c is 90°.

narration: Start with the longest side, five, as the possible hypotenuse. The squares of three and four add to twenty-five, exactly five squared. The converse of Pythagoras therefore proves the opposite angle is a right angle. No right-angle mark is assumed before carrying out the test.
